questions.question:
Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10.
(a) Give the six-figure grid reference for spot height .437 in the southeastern part of the map extract.
(b) Aman, a local craftsman, wants to sell his product to a large gathering to earn money instantly.
1. Which settlement should he go to?
2. Name the month in which he should visit the settlement named by you above.
questions.solution: (a) 673295. (b) 1. Pamera (6233), a large settlement. 2. March, as an annual fair is organised in the month of March.
questions.figure_desc: Survey of India toposheet extract G43S10 (not reproduced)

questions.question:
(a) On which bank of the Sukli nadi is the settlement of Pamera situated?
(b) Identify the settlement pattern seen in the grid square 6732.
questions.solution: (a) Pamera is situated on the right bank of the Sukli Nadi. (b) The settlement pattern in grid square 6732 is dispersed.
questions.figure_desc: Survey of India toposheet extract G43S10 (not reproduced)

questions.question:
Roshan, while travelling from Sirori to Tokra, observed that the surface water sources are dry except for the reservoir near Tokra.
(a) What according to you may be the reason for the presence of water in the reservoir in 6832 near Tokra settlement?
(b) State whether this reservoir is an artificial or natural source of water.
questions.solution: (a) The embankments made obstruct the flow of water and help to store water for the dry months. (b) The reservoir is an artificial source of water.

marking_points.point: Embankments obstruct flow of water / store water for dry months

questions.figure_desc: Survey of India toposheet extract G43S10 (not reproduced)

questions.question:
(a) What is the direct distance between Gulabganj to Pithapura? Give your answer in kilometre.
(b) Mention the compass direction of Pithapura from Gulabganj.
questions.solution: (a) The direct distance is approximately 3 km. (b) Pithapura lies to the Northeast of Gulabganj.
questions.figure_desc: Survey of India toposheet extract G43S10 (not reproduced)

questions.question:
(a) Name two man-made features seen in the grid square 6534.
(b) Define contour interval.
questions.solution: (a) Any two: metalled roads, cart tracks, temples, permanent huts. (b) Contour interval is the vertical difference in elevation between adjacent contour lines on a topographic map. In this map the contour interval is 20 metres.

marking_points.point: Any one correct man-made feature (e.g. metalled road, cart track, temple, permanent huts)
Contour interval = vertical difference in elevation between adjacent contour lines

questions.figure_desc: Survey of India toposheet extract G43S10 (not reproduced)

Nathu La pass: on the Sikkim-Tibet (India-China) border, east of Gangtok (about 27.4 deg N, 88.8 deg E). Mark it on the north-east border of Sikkim and label 'Nathu La'.

questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). The Malabar Coast: the coastal plain along the Arabian Sea covering most of Kerala (southern part of the western coastal plain). Shade the Kerala coastal strip and label 'Malabar Coast'.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label Digboi.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Digboi: oil town in Tinsukia district, Upper Assam, north-east India (about 27.4 deg N, 95.6 deg E), near Dibrugarh. Mark a dot and label 'Digboi'.

North-East Monsoon (Retreating Monsoon) winds: arrows from the north-east, over the Bay of Bengal, pointing south-west towards the Coromandel (Tamil Nadu) coast. Draw arrows and label 'NE Monsoon'.

Satpura range: a chain of hills running east-west in central India, south of the Narmada river, from Gujarat through Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra to Chhattisgarh (Maikal range / Amarkantak). Mark it south of the Narmada and label 'Satpura'.

questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Visakhapatnam: port on the east coast of Andhra Pradesh, Bay of Bengal (about 17.7 deg N, 83.3 deg E). Mark a dot on the coast and label 'Visakhapatnam'.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Mumbai receives more rainfall than Pune.
Reason (R): Mumbai gets rain from Arabian Sea branch of southwest monsoon.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation for (A).

questions.solution: Option (a). Mumbai is on the windward side of the Western Ghats, directly exposed to the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon, whereas Pune on the leeward side receives less rainfall.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of soils displays similar characteristics in terms of their colour and texture?
questions.solution: Option (c) Red soil and laterite soil. Both are rich in iron oxide giving a reddish colour, and have a coarse texture and are well-drained.

questions.question: The type of natural vegetation shown in the picture given below is found in:
questions.solution: Option (c) Tropical evergreen. The tall, dense trees with multiple canopy layers indicate tropical evergreen forest, found in regions with about 200 cm rainfall and high humidity such as the Western Ghats and Northeastern India.
questions.figure_desc: Picture of natural vegetation: tall dense trees with multiple canopy layers (tropical evergreen forest)

questions.question: Which of the following prevents wastage of water?
questions.solution: Option (c) Sprinkler. Sprinkler irrigation distributes water efficiently, reducing evaporation and runoff.

questions.question: Balaghat : Manganese :: Mumbai High : ____________________
questions.solution: Option (d) Petroleum. Balaghat produces manganese; Mumbai High is an offshore oil field producing petroleum.

questions.question: A microbiological process that loosens the bark of a crop and facilitates removal of fibre from the stalk:
questions.solution: Option (c) Retting. Retting: microorganisms break down pectin binding fibres to the stalk (jute, flax, hemp).

questions.question: Which industry amongst the following has revolutionised the lifestyle of the Indian masses in recent years?
questions.solution: Option (b) Electronic. Electronics industry introduced mobile phones, internet, computers and digital transactions.

questions.question: Which of the following household products is associated with the petrochemical industry?
questions.solution: Option (d) Plastic mug. Plastic is made from polymers derived from petrochemicals.

questions.question: Raman, a dairy farmer in Ludhiana, supplies milk within the city on a daily basis. Which mode of transport is he most likely to use?
questions.solution: Option (b) Roadway. Road transport is the most flexible for local door-to-door daily delivery.

questions.question: The collection of discarded materials and converting them into useful products is:
questions.solution: Option (a) Recycling. Recycling reuses waste materials to create new products.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
'Severe cyclonic storms are often formed over the Bay of Bengal during the retreating monsoon season'.
(a) Name two states that are affected by tropical cyclones on the eastern coast of India.
(b) The temperate cyclones cause less damage than the tropical cyclones. Give any two points to support this statement.
questions.solution: (a) Odisha and Andhra Pradesh (also e.g. Tamil Nadu, West Bengal). (b) Weaker winds: temperate cyclones have wind speeds of 30-60 km/h whereas tropical cyclones can exceed 200 km/h. Less storm surge: tropical cyclones bring intense storm surges causing severe flooding, while temperate cyclones usually cause moderate rainfall and winds.

marking_points.point: Two eastern-coast states, e.g. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh
Point 1: weaker winds (30-60 km/h vs over 200 km/h)

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
(a) Name the local wind that causes rainfall in the states of Assam and West Bengal in the month of April.
(b) How is this rainfall beneficial for the states mentioned above?
questions.solution: (a) Nor'westers (Kalbaisakhi), violent thunderstorms bringing pre-monsoon rainfall in April-May. (b) The rain benefits paddy, jute and tea plantations; it gives temporary relief from summer heat by cooling temperatures before the monsoon.

marking_points.point: Benefit to crops (paddy, jute, tea) or relief from heat

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
concepts: SW vs NE monsoon wind direction diagrams
questions.question:
With reference to Figure A and Figure B given below, answer the questions that follow:
(a) Name the winds shown by arrows in Figure A and Figure B.
(b) How is the wind shown in Figure A different from the one shown in Figure B?
questions.solution: (a) Figure A: Southwest Monsoon winds. Figure B: Northeast Monsoon winds. (b) Figure A blows from the sea (Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal) towards the land, bringing moisture and rainfall during June-September. Figure B blows from the land towards the sea during October-December, carries less moisture and brings rainfall mainly to the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu).

marking_points.point: Difference in direction (sea to land vs land to sea)
Difference in season/moisture/rainfall (Jun-Sep moist heavy rain vs Oct-Dec less moisture, Coromandel coast)

questions.figure_desc: Two India maps: Figure A shows arrows of wind blowing from the sea onto land (southwest monsoon); Figure B shows arrows blowing from land towards the sea (northeast monsoon)

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
Study the climate data of station X and answer the following questions:
Month: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, June, July, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec
Temp (C): 24.0, 25.4, 26.7, 28.3, 30.0, 28.9, 27.6, 27.4, 27.3, 27.1, 27.0, 25.0
Rainfall (cm): 0.25, 0.25, -, -, 1.75, 50.2, 61.0, 37.0, 27.0, 4.75, 1.50, -
(a) What is the annual range of temperature for station X?
(b) Which is the wettest month?
(c) Name the wind which brings rainfall for station X during the rainy season.
questions.solution: (a) Annual range = highest (30.0 C, May) - lowest (24.0 C, January) = 6.0 C. (b) July, with the highest rainfall of 61.0 cm. (c) Southwest Monsoon winds.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
The Ganga Plain is known for its fertile soil. It is often referred to as the food bowl of India. This region supports a variety of crops such as rice, wheat, pulses, jute and sugarcane.
(a) Name the soil that is found in large parts of Ganga plain.
(b) Give two properties of this soil which helps it to produce a variety of crops.
questions.solution: (a) Alluvial soil. (b) It contains potash, phosphoric acid and lime, making it highly fertile; it retains water, making it suitable for irrigation and multiple cropping.

marking_points.point: Property 1: rich in potash, phosphoric acid, lime (fertile)
Property 2: retains water / suitable for irrigation and multiple cropping

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
(a) What is meant by soil erosion?
(b) Name any two agents of soil erosion.
questions.solution: (a) Soil erosion is the removal of the top fertile layer of soil by natural agents like wind and water, leading to land degradation. (b) Any two: water (runoff, heavy rain, floods); strong winds; human activities such as deforestation, construction and unreasonable farming.

marking_points.point: Definition: removal of top fertile layer of soil by wind/water

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
Give a geographical reason to explain each of the following:
(a) Soil conservation is the need of the hour.
(b) Red soil has a poor water retention capacity.
(c) Laterite soils are infertile.
questions.solution: (a) Soil is a non-renewable resource; deforestation, overgrazing and intensive farming cause degradation, so conservation is essential for productivity and to prevent desertification. (b) Red soil is porous and lacks humus and clay, so it cannot retain moisture for long. (c) Laterite areas receive heavy rainfall which causes leaching and loss of nutrients such as nitrogen and potassium.

marking_points.point: (a) Non-renewable resource / degradation by deforestation, overgrazing
(c) Heavy rain causes leaching of nutrients

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
concepts: black soil formation and moisture retention
questions.question:
With reference to black soil of India, answer the following questions.
(a) How is this soil formed?
(b) How is this soil able to retain moisture for a long period?
(c) Mention any two minerals present in this soil.
questions.solution: (a) Weathering of volcanic rocks, particularly basaltic lava of the Deccan Plateau. (b) It is clayey, so it absorbs and retains moisture for a long time. (c) Iron and magnesium carbonate (also lime, alumina).

marking_points.point: Formed by weathering of volcanic/basaltic lava (Deccan)

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
India has lost 2.33 million hectares of tree cover since the year 2000. This is equivalent to a six per cent decrease in tree cover during this period. (Source: The Indian Express, 12.04.2024)
(a) Mention any two causes of the decrease in the forest cover of India.
(b) Name a conservation method that may be used to help in increasing the forest cover.
questions.solution: (a) Deforestation for agriculture and urbanisation; uncontrolled forest fires. (b) Afforestation (planting new trees) or reforestation (replanting in deforested areas).

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question: Mention the climatic condition suitable for the development of tropical evergreen forest.
questions.solution: High rainfall (over 200 cm annually) and high temperatures (25-27 C) throughout the year.

marking_points.point: High temperature 25-27 C throughout the year

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question: State any three differences between tropical deciduous and tropical desert vegetation.
questions.solution: Annual rainfall: deciduous 100-200 cm; desert less than 50 cm. Trees: deciduous trees shed leaves in dry season (sal, teak); desert has cactus and thorny bushes adapted to dry conditions. Location: deciduous in central and eastern India; desert in Rajasthan, Gujarat.

marking_points.point: Difference in rainfall (100-200 cm vs under 50 cm)
Difference in type of vegetation (sal/teak shed leaves vs cactus/thorny bushes)
Difference in location (central/eastern India vs Rajasthan/Gujarat)

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
(a) Give any two reasons for the great diversity of natural vegetation in India.
(b) How do the forests help in maintenance of air quality?
questions.solution: (a) Varied climate (tropical to temperate and alpine); diverse landforms (mountains, plateaus, plains, coasts). (b) Forests absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, reducing air pollution; trees also trap dust and pollutants.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention any one advantage and any one disadvantage of well irrigation.
questions.solution: Advantage: wells can be dug easily with low initial investment, accessible to farmers. Disadvantage: can deplete groundwater if overused; needs investment for digging and pumps.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Suggest any two measures to overcome scarcity of water in the metropolitan cities of India.
questions.solution: Rainwater harvesting (collect and store rainwater from buildings and open spaces); recycling wastewater (treat and reuse for non-drinking purposes like irrigation and cleaning).

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: tank vs canal vs tube well irrigation conditions
questions.question:
Give one reason to explain each of the following:
(a) Tank irrigation is NOT common in Northern India.
(b) Canal irrigation is important in Punjab.
(c) All farmers do not use tube well irrigation even if the geographical condition is favourable.
questions.solution: (a) Northern India has flat terrain and perennial rivers (canals suit it); tanks are common in regions of uneven topography like Southern India. (b) Punjab has a network of rivers and fertile plains, ideal for canals. (c) High cost of installation and maintenance prevents small farmers; groundwater depletion in some regions.

marking_points.point: (b) Network of rivers and fertile plains
(c) High installation/maintenance cost or groundwater depletion

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: State any three objectives of rainwater harvesting.
questions.solution: To conserve water (reduce dependence on surface and groundwater); to recharge groundwater levels; to reduce waterlogging and urban floods.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With the rising price of fossil fuel every passing day, it is very important to develop non-conventional energy resource. (Bulletin - Department of Non-conventional Sources of Energy)
(a) Name a non-conventional energy source that can be harnessed by taking advantage of India's vast coastline.
(b) State one advantage of using geothermal energy.
questions.solution: (a) Tidal energy (e.g. Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Khambhat, Sunderbans); wave energy also acceptable. (b) Geothermal energy is renewable and eco-friendly, produces no greenhouse gases and gives a constant supply.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
(a) How is Biogas formed?
(b) Mention any one advantage of Biogas over other non-conventional energy resources.
questions.solution: (a) Anaerobic decomposition of organic matter (cow dung, agricultural waste, sewage) by bacteria in the absence of oxygen. (b) Helps waste management, clean renewable energy, reduces pollution and yields organic fertiliser (any one).

marking_points.point: Anaerobic decomposition of organic waste by bacteria without oxygen

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give a reason for each of the following.
(a) Iron ore is called a versatile mineral.
(b) Windmills set up on agricultural lands are beneficial to farmers.
(c) Coal is the most preferred source of energy in Indian industries.
questions.solution: (a) It is used to produce steel, essential for construction, machinery, automobile and other industries. (b) Windmills generate renewable energy and give farmers additional income from electricity on unused land. (c) Coal is abundantly available in India and relatively cheap.

marking_points.point: (a) Used to make steel for many industries

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the picture of an energy generation plant:
(a) Identify the type of energy being generated in the picture given above.
(b) State why this type of energy is cheaper in the long run.
(c) Name a power project associated with the generation of this energy in the northern part of India.
questions.solution: (a) Hydroelectric energy (from flowing water). (b) It relies on water, a renewable resource, and once the dam is built operating costs are minimal compared to fossil-fuel plants. (c) Bhakra Nangal project on the Sutlej.

marking_points.point: Renewable water / low operating cost after dam built

questions.figure_desc: Picture of a dam / hydroelectric power plant generating energy from flowing water

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention two climatic conditions that favour the cultivation of groundnut.
questions.solution: Warm temperature (20-30 C) and moderate annual rainfall (50-75 cm).

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give any two reasons why Maharashtra has emerged as an important sugarcane producing state.
questions.solution: Fertile well-drained black soil; developed irrigation facilities in river valleys ensuring reliable water supply.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give one reason to explain each of the following:
(a) Trees are planted in between the rows of coffee plants.
(b) Cotton cultivation requires plenty of cheap labour.
(c) Hill slopes are best suited for tea cultivation.
questions.solution: (a) Coffee is shade-loving and needs protection from direct sunlight and strong winds. (b) Sowing, weeding, picking and ginning are labour-intensive. (c) Tea needs well-drained soil; slopes prevent waterlogging.

marking_points.point: (a) Shade / protection from sun and wind

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Explain the following:
(a) Mixed farming
(b) Zayad
(c) Transplantation
questions.solution: (a) Growing crops and raising livestock on the same farm. (b) Short cropping season in summer between rabi and kharif; e.g. watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon. (c) Seedlings are raised in nurseries and then transferred to the main field; e.g. rice.

marking_points.point: Mixed farming: crops and livestock on same farm
Zayad: short summer season between rabi and kharif
Transplantation: seedlings from nursery moved to field

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: State any two factors that are responsible for the growth of the cotton textile industry in Kolkata.
questions.solution: Availability of raw cotton (surrounding regions and imports); cheap and skilled labour; port facility for import of raw cotton and export of finished goods (any two).

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: 'Karnataka is the leading state for silk production in India'. Give any two reasons to justify the above statement.
questions.solution: Favourable warm humid climate for silkworm rearing; extensive mulberry plantations providing food for silkworms.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: Bhilai steel plant raw material sources
questions.question:
(a) Name the Iron and Steel industry located at Chhattisgarh.
(b) From where does the industry named by you above get its supply of the following?
1. Iron ore
2. Coal
questions.solution: (a) Bhilai Steel Plant. (b) 1. Iron ore from Dalli-Rajhara mines (Chhattisgarh). 2. Coal from Korba and Jharia coalfields.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: coal tar by-products of coal-based industry
questions.question:
Raghav has been given a project by his teacher in which he has to write about the by-products of an industry that is used for preparing shoe polish, carbon paper and cardboard.
(a) Which industry will he be writing about?
(b) Name any two by-products of the industry mentioned by you.
questions.solution: (a) Petrochemical industry. (b) Any two by-products of petroleum refining, for example paraffin wax (used in candles, shoe polish, carbon paper and wax-coated cardboard), bitumen/asphalt, petroleum jelly, lubricating oils.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Why is a well-developed transport network important for India?
questions.solution: It enhances trade, connectivity and economic development by ensuring efficient movement of goods, people and services; it promotes industrial growth and strengthens national integration.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention any two advantages of road transport.
questions.solution: Door-to-door service with flexibility; connectivity to remote hilly and rural areas where rail or air is not feasible.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Name the following:
(a) The mode of transport that ensures comfortable journey, especially for elders and children.
(b) The highway connecting Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat.
(c) The cheapest means of transport for bulky goods.

answer_items.prompt: Mode of transport comfortable for elders and children
Cheapest means of transport for bulky goods

questions.solution: (a) Railways. (b) National Highway 27, the East-West Corridor. (c) Water transport (inland waterways and coastal shipping).

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give a reason for each of the following.
(a) Airways are the most efficient mode of transport to connect Northeast India with the rest of the country.
(b) Railways are easily developed in the Northern Plains of India.
(c) Rivers of peninsular India are NOT ideal for inland water transport.
questions.solution: (a) Northeast India has challenging terrain of dense forests, hills and rivers making road and rail development difficult; airways are fastest and most reliable. (b) Northern Plains are flat with fertile soil, so laying tracks is easy and cheap; high population density ensures demand. (c) Peninsular rivers are seasonal, rain-fed with rocky beds, waterfalls and rapids, unsuitable for navigation.

marking_points.point: (b) Flat land, cheap tracks / dense population
(c) Seasonal rivers, rocky beds, waterfalls and rapids

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
(a) Give a reason for a substantial rise of E-waste in India.
(b) What is dumping?
questions.solution: (a) Rapid technological advancement, increasing consumerism and shorter product lifecycles; lack of proper disposal mechanisms (any one). (b) Dumping is the indiscriminate disposal of waste in open areas, landfills or water bodies without proper treatment or recycling, causing pollution.

marking_points.point: One valid reason for rise of e-waste

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: personal waste management actions with examples
questions.question:
'You cannot protect environment unless you empower people, you inform them and help them to understand that these resources are their own, that they must protect them.' - Wangari Maathai (Nobel Prize 2004).
As a responsible student how would you contribute to reduce and manage the waste generated in your surroundings. Explain by giving suitable examples.
questions.solution: Any two: practise and promote the 3Rs (reusable bags and bottles, repairing items, segregating waste); awareness campaigns and workshops on segregation, recycling and composting (e.g. donating old clothes, waste segregation bins in school); composting units in school and homes; clean-up drives in neighbourhoods, parks and beaches.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the 3Rs, give a term that best describes each of the following:
(a) An empty soft drink can is used as a pen stand.
(b) Old scrap papers are used to manufacture handmade paper.
(c) No food is wasted in the household.

answer_items.prompt: Empty soft drink can used as a pen stand
Old scrap paper used to make handmade paper
No food wasted in the household

questions.solution: (a) Reuse (b) Recycle (c) Reduce

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Organic manure, plastic ban, waste handling
questions.question:
Give a reason for the following statements:
(a) Organic manure should replace chemical fertilisers.
(b) There should be a ban on the use of polythene and plastic products.
(c) Manual handling of waste must be avoided.
questions.solution: (a) Organic manure is eco-friendly, improves soil fertility and causes no soil degradation or water pollution, unlike chemical fertilisers. (b) Synthetic polymers do not disintegrate, damage soil and water, cause wildlife deaths and choke drains causing urban flooding. (c) Workers can come into contact with harmful substances, toxic chemicals and germs causing severe health problems.

marking_points.point: (c) Exposure to toxic substances and germs
